summary: A scholar of Indology and philosophy, Nobuyuki Watase completed a master's program at Kyoto University around 1964–1966. He served as professor at Tokai University from circa 1987 to 2007 and as president of Kobe Shukugawa Gakuin University circa 2007–2010.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Nobuyuki Yamagiwa taught Shayne Clarke. He served as full-time lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 1997–2002) and as professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Nobuyuki Yoshimoto studied at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and doctoral supervisor Genjun Sasaki (1972). He served as a JSPS fellow in 1972 and held assistant, lecturer, and research appointments at Otani University.

Nolan Pliny Jacobson worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies, earning degrees from Emory University and the University of Chicago (Ph.D. c. 1940–1948). His career included teaching at several colleges, notably as professor of philosophy and religion at Winthrop University (1954–1974).

Noopur Shalini works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at NIFT, IGNOU, Ningbo University, and the University of Mumbai, and held a post in the Department of Archaeology at Zhejiang University in 2023.

A scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics, Nora Kershaw Chadwick studied at Newnham College, Cambridge (c. 1911–1915). She later held posts at the University of St Andrews (c. 1919–1923) and the University of Cambridge (c. 1950–1958).

A scholar of philosophy and religious studies, Norbert M. Samuelson studied at Northwestern, Hebrew Union College, and Indiana University under Shlomo Pines. He served as professor at Temple University (1975–1998) and held the Grossman Chair at Arizona State University.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Noriaki Hakamaya studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Shun'ei Hirai and Zuiho Yamaguchi. He was a longtime professor at Komazawa University (1985–2011) and held visiting professorships at UW–Madison.

Noriaki Hosoda works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held posts as assistant (attested 1986) and associate professor (attested 2003) at Hokkaido University, and as professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).
Specializing in Indology and Buddhist studies, Noriaki Inoue studied at Taisho University until 1953. He later served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1982).

A Buddhist studies scholar, Norihiko Tanaka studied at Osaka Kyoiku University, Bukkyo University, and Visva-Bharati University. He spent his career at Bukkyo University, advancing from lecturer in 1976 to professor in 1994, and serving as professor emeritus from 2015 to 2021.
Specializing in linguistics and Indology, Norihiko Uchida studied under Yutaka Ochihara. He held an assistant post at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1962).
Norihiro Matsuura works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. As of 2026, he is attested as faculty at Otani University and the Otani Academic Society.

Norihisa Baba is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo under Masahiro Shimoda. He has served as professor at the University of Tokyo's Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia since 2018.

Norio Koyama specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami, and served as professor at Taisho University (attested 2014) and head of the Matsunami Seiren Sensei Koki Kinenkai (attested 2007).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, Noritoshi Aramaki earned doctoral credentials from Kyoto University. He taught at Kyoto University, Osaka University, and Otani University, and served as director at Kyoto Koka Women's University around 2006.

Noriyuki Kudo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at Bukkyo University. He has held positions as lecturer at Bukkyo University and associate professor at Soka University and its International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology.

Norman Brooke Jopson specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Cambridge, Vienna (under Paul Kretschmer), Charles University, and Saint Petersburg. He served as Reader at King's College London (1922) and Professor of Comparative Philology at Cambridge (1937–1955).

A scholar of Indology and religious studies, Norman Cutler studied at the University of Michigan, the University of Washington, and the University of Chicago under A. K. Ramanujan. He served as assistant professor at the University of Chicago from circa 1979 to 2002.

Norman Fischer works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned degrees from Colgate University, University of Iowa, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union, studied under Mel Weitsman and Richard Baker, and founded the Everyday Zen Foundation in 2000.
